messages:
sophia: Heads-up — we've got a customer escalation: p99 latency up ~3x starting ~23:10 UTC, correlated with GPU OOMs on pool-12. Customer repros with long-context generation (~16k tokens). Logs show repeated OOM + retry/backoff which spikes tail latency. Filing thread to coordinate mitigations and root cause.

vikram: which model and fleet? is this hosted or dedicated? any recent rollout?

sophia: Dedicated pool-12 (us-west-2), running rwd-open-13b-v2 (fp16). No infra rollout in the last 6h. Support attached customer case: request rates are normal but context lengths jumped.

jorge: pinging pool owners @vikram — infra-bot alerted at 23:08:

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu_mem_fragmentation_pct=86.3, gpu_free=1.2GB, pool=pool-12, nodes_affected=3 (suspected KV growth).

danielle: can you paste the OOM stack/log snippet? need to know if it's allocator OOM or CUDA OOM. Also if KV cache is growing unbounded per-request.

sophia: snippet below (from runtime-host-12):

```
[23:07:58] ERROR runtime: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[23:07:58] WARN runtime: attempt to evict KV cache entries failed (evicted=0)
[23:08:01] INFO runtime: retrying request, backoff=200ms
[23:08:05] ERROR runtime: allocation failed: CUDA OOM while allocating 1.3GB (requested=1384120320)
[23:08:07] INFO allocator: total_gpu=40GB used=38.7GB fragments=3.2GB (8%)
[23:08:07] INFO kv: kv_cache_size=14.2GB kv_entries=18.1M per_request_growth=~40KB
```

danielle: OK, looks like both fragmentation and KV growth. per_request_growth ~40KB implies long prefixes with lots of key material. Quick mitigation options:
- temporarily route heavy-context traffic to smaller quantized model (rwd-open-13b-q4f32) or rwd-open-7b to reduce working set
- force KV pruning / trim on pool-12 nodes
- throttle max_context for that customer via project-level policy

vikram: we should do the least invasive first. Can we do a KV trim + throttle while we investigate allocator tunables?

jorge: I ran admin dry-run on host-12: kv_trim shows reclaimable ~3.8GB across shards. Command below (requires admin role):

```bash
# preview
/opt/redwood/bin/kv_trim --pool pool-12 --dry-run --threshold 0.6
# apply
/opt/redwood/bin/kv_trim --pool pool-12 --threshold 0.6 --concurrency 4
```

sophia: doing kv_trim now on two affected nodes. Also notifying support to apply project-level throttle to the offending API key (low risk).

support-bot: Case #C-21345: customer experiencing p99 spikes. Support reduced max_context to 8192 for their key and requested mitigation steps.

infra-bot: action: kv_trim applied on host-12, host-14 — reclaimed 3.1GB. Post-trim gpu_free increased to ~4.0GB, fragmentation down to 72%.

vikram: good. Any immediate change to p99?

sophia: early telemetry: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s on affected nodes, overall pool p99 still ~1.3s because other nodes still catching up. p95 improved marginally.

danielle: next steps: longer-term fix — allocator tuning + runtime config: enable jemalloc purge cadence and reduce small-bin retention. Suggested MALLOC_CONF: "oversize_threshold:1,background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:15000,muzzy_decay_ms:15000". This reduces fragmentation at cost of slightly higher CPU/alloc churn. Need canary.

jorge: runtime also has an option kv_shrink=true which will aggressively drop least-recently-used KV entries beyond a soft limit. We can enable kv_shrink for pool-12 as a temporary policy. Patch below (runtime config yaml snippet):

```yaml
pools:
  pool-12:
    kv_shrink: true
    kv_shrink_threshold: 0.7   # shrink when >70% usage
    max_concurrent_trim: 2
```

vikram: agreed on staged approach: 1) throttle customer + kv_trim (done) 2) enable kv_shrink for pool-12 (no restart) 3) canary jemalloc MALLOC_CONF on 10% of nodes with rolling restart 4) evaluate batcher size and max_context enforcement in API layer.

sophia: I've enabled kv_shrink on pool-12 via runtime feature-flag (no restart). Monitoring.

infra-bot: automatic metric bump: pool-12 kv_cache_size trending down to 9.7GB after kv_shrink and trims. fragmentation=65%.

danielle: note on jemalloc: per-node change will require service restart to pick up MALLOC_CONF env. Plan a rolling restart with canary=1, wait 30m metrics, then continue. Also add allocator metrics to our dashboards (arena_count, retained_bytes, active:dirty ratio).

vikram: repro steps to validate locally (devbox):
1) spawn request with 16k tokens to rwd-open-13b-v2 against pool-12 dev endpoint
2) watch /metrics for kv_cache_size and gpu_free
3) run kv_trim and observe frees
\Example curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://dev-runtime.us-west-2.redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-13b-v2","prompt":"<16k tokens...>","max_tokens":8000}'
```

jorge: I executed the curl against canary node and reproduced OOM within ~2 requests. After kv_trim + kv_shrink, canary handled same load for 20 requests without OOM. Captured heap/proc metrics to /var/log/runtime/oom-debug.log and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/pool-12/oom-debug-2456789012.log).

sophia: TL;DR: immediate mitigation worked (kv_trim + kv_shrink + project throttle). Medium-term: jemalloc tuning + add allocator dashboards + enforce soft max_context per project. Long-term: consider per-request KV caps or streaming prefix-only KV to reduce memory pressure.

vikram: can we schedule the jemalloc canary+restart in the next maintenance window (00:30 UTC)? I'll own the rollout. oncall — can you monitor the canary and be ready to rollback?

oncall: oncall here, will monitor. set alert for gpu_free < 2GB and p99 > 2s. I have a rollback runbook if needed.

sophia: assigning owner: vikram leads jemalloc canary; danielle will prepare dashboard patches and runbook; jorge will follow up on KV heuristics; oncall monitors. Closing this thread after postmortem notes drafted. :thumbsup:
